question: Hostile audit, CYCLE 1, of law L-r GPU0 NEVER SURPRISES A RUN (Protocol Pulse video pipeline; orchestrator order 2026-11-12 '01:55' B). Background: GPU0 (24564 MiB, nvidia-smi index 0) is shared with an Ollama server (gemma3:27b, ~20.5 GB resident); GPU1 is quarantined. On Nov 12 a pinned run died because the preflight left gemma3:27b resident and Whisper hit CUDA out-of-memory, and the HOLD read 'pinned decision rejected: R-iKNbc7-zk: transcription failed' (the OOM was swallowed and renamed). The law, verbatim items: (1) ONE owner: every code path that loads anything on GPU0 takes the gpu0.py lease first; no lease, no load. (2) ONE model at a time by construction: a single swap_to(model) unloads whatever is resident (Ollama keep_alive=0 + confirm via the GPU0 listener, torch empty_cache, delete the Whisper object), then VERIFIES by nvidia-smi that free memory >= the incoming model's known requirement plus margin before loading; every stage calls it, nothing calls a loader directly; the preflight leaves GPU0 as empty as it found it and asserts that. (3) Bounded self-heal: on CUDA OOM, release everything this run owns, wait until nvidia-smi shows the memory free (timeout), retry the SAME step ONCE, log both attempts in PROVENANCE; a second failure is a HOLD naming every GPU0 process (pid, name, MiB); an OOM never surfaces as a different error. (4) Foreign processes: at run start and before every swap, a process not holding the lease using GPU0 memory = HOLD naming it; nothing killed; GPU1 untouched. (5) Tests: must-fails with a real dummy allocation before each stage; a back-to-back double run with a per-stage peak GPU0 table in every REPORT.md. Design (pipeline/gpu0.py, new): flock lease (custody = an inherited descriptor whose open file description holds the flock, probed with a non-blocking flock on our own fds); require() also demands CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; Model objects (one per key) load only via swap_to and are deleted by any later swap; Gpu0Stop is a BaseException so `except Exception` swallow sites cannot rename it; guard()/guard_iter() convert CUDA OOM inside model calls and lazy decoding; is_oom() also reads CalledProcessError stderr (NVENC); REQUIREMENT_MIB measured by pipeline/measure_gpu0.py; run_fresh.Run._attempts implements item 3; the four former swallow sites re-raise a raw OOM as GpuOOM. FIND, with file and line, only what you can verify from the diff (say 'uncertain' otherwise): (a) any GPU0 load path that bypasses swap_to/require; (b) any way an OOM or another GPU0 stop can still surface as a different error or be swallowed; (c) races or holes in the lease/custody logic (held(), lease(), the wrapper's fd 8, children, threads); (d) any way swap_to can declare GPU0 free when it is not, or refuse forever when it is; (e) whether the foreign-process rule can mis-classify (ancestors/descendants/Ollama runners) in a way that lets a foreign job share GPU0 or HOLDs a clean run; (f) whether the retry in Run._attempts is bounded and logs both attempts, and whether retrying a stage can double side effects that a gate later trusts; (g) whether anything changes what a gate, the sentence lock, pin validation or release_auth accepts (it must not); (h) test weaknesses (stubs that hide the behaviour, must-fails that are not load-bearing). No praise.
